subject: Novapay production latency & errors — executive summary and ops plan
messages:
From: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@novapay.com>
To: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: infra@novapay.com, support@novapay.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: Production request latency spike + 5xx errors (Novapay)

Chloe / Sergio —

We started seeing a big uptick in request latency and sporadic 5xx rates hitting our Redwood endpoints around 13:40 PST. Our load balancers show a sudden queueing increase and several customer-facing payments are failing (time window: 13:40–14:00). This is impacting checkout flows — roughly 8% of requests are timing out or returning 5xx currently.

We restarted a few services on our side but problem persists. Novapay is at risk for the morning batch settlement if this continues. Can you confirm whether there are any network-level changes on your side (VPC peering, NAT changes, or proxy updates) or any regional throttles?

Attached: small pcap and high-level logs from our gateway.

Thanks — please escalate.

— Alyssa
Alyssa Park
Sr. Infra Ops, Novapay

Attachments: novapay_pcap_summary.txt (text), customer_gateway_logs.txt (text)
From: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@novapay.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 14:11:38 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: Production request latency spike + 5xx errors (Novapay)

Alyssa —

Thanks for the quick heads up and for the pcap. We’re treating this as an incident. I’ve looped in Sergio (networks) and Vivek for exec visibility. Initial checks show elevated tail latency on the egress cluster serving your tenant and an increase in proxy 502s between 13:35–13:55.

Immediate next steps we are running now:
- Sergio will pull VPC peering/route tables and NAT gateway metrics for your region.
- I’m requesting the runtime traces and proxy logs for the affected nodes.
- We will temporarily route Novapay traffic to the secondary capacity pool to mitigate impact if we see sustained errors.

Can you confirm whether you pushed any changes to your egress ACLs or changed DNS TTLs in the last hour? If you can provide a timeline of any infra jobs, that will help.

I’ll follow up with a short exec brief in ~30m.

— Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0132
From: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@novapay.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 14:24:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: Production request latency spike + 5xx errors (Novapay)

Quick triage notes — collected and attaching runtime trace.

Findings so far:
- VPC peering health for Novapay’s account shows intermittent route flaps between 13:33–13:48 (BGP flap counters incremented on two spokes).
- Proxy (ingress-edge) CPU and queueing spiked concurrently; proxy returned surge of 502/504 for inflight streams when KV cache miss rates increased.
- DNS: no global change, but we see increased NXDOMAIN and retry storms from a small subset of Novapay edge nodes — TTLs look normal but client resolvers issued retries aggressively.

Attached: redwood_runtime_trace.json (filtered), novapay_pcap_summary.txt (they provided). I’ve opened INF-9482 in Jira to track network-level remediation.

Immediate mitigations applied:
1) Rerouted Novapay to secondary dedicated pool (manual failover) — reduced 5xx from ~8% to ~1.2% for a short window.
2) Throttle applied to aggressive client resolvers to prevent retry amplification.
3) We flagged suspicious BGP peers and asked infra to hold any peering changes.

Next ask for Novapay: can you share resolver IP ranges that are issuing retries so we can target throttles without impacting legitimate users?

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_runtime_trace.json (json), mitigation_checklist.pdf (pdf)
From: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Executive brief — Novapay incident & short-term plan

Vivek / Lauren —

Summary for execs: Novapay production saw a sharp latency and 5xx spike at ~13:35 PST tied to a combination of (1) intermittent BGP route flaps affecting a subset of egress spokes and (2) retry amplification from customer resolvers causing proxy queue saturation. We completed an emergency manual failover to a secondary capacity pool which materially reduced errors, and we applied targeted throttles to noisy resolvers.

Impact: checkout failures for some customers, estimated revenue exposure for the 20-minute window. We currently rate at ~1% 5xx after mitigations.

Requested asks:
- Approve a short-term SLA credit for Novapay for the event window (they are asking for a credit to avoid contract churn).
- Approve priority remediation resources to replace flapping BGP peer and harden proxy retry-handling (2 engineers x 2 days).

I’ve attached the runtime trace and checklist. If you want, I can call into a quick sync with Novapay at 16:00.

— Chloe

Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: Production request latency spike + 5xx errors (Novapay) — mitigation update

Alyssa —

Quick postmortem and next steps: our incident review shows a compound failure (BGP instability + retry amplification) that produced proxy queue saturation on a small fraction of your traffic. Actions taken:

- Immediate: manual failover to secondary capacity pool at 13:50 reduced 5xx to ~1% and removed high tail latency for most traffic.
- Short-term (next 48 hours): we will replace the flapping peer, apply permanent retry-backoff logic in the proxy, and add targeted resolver throttles.
- Compensation: we are prepared to issue a partial SLA credit for the 20-minute impact window as a gesture while remediation completes (I will follow up with finance for the exact credit amount).
- Follow-up: postmortem writeup and timeline posted to the shared drive: https://drive.redwood.com/novapay/incident-2026-12-01

Can you confirm the resolver IP ranges you saw sending retries and whether you shifted any DNS TTLs during the event?

We’ll keep you updated hourly until the permanent fix is in production. Thanks again for escalating and for the pcap — that enabled faster correlation.

— Chloe
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com

Attachments: mitigation_checklist.pdf (pdf)
